actor_id.description: ActorID is null for entries the server wrote itself.

details.description:
Details holds the sanitized request, a before snapshot and the changed
fields; its shape depends on the action.

next_before.description:
NextBefore is the value of the before parameter that fetches the next
page; null on the last page.

confirmation_sent.description:
ConfirmationSent is only present in the answer to PUT /api/users/me/email
for a new address: false when the address was saved but the
confirmation mail was refused (too many mails or SMTP failure), so the
client can offer to send it again. Omitted when no mail was due.

email.description:
Email is the caller's own address; omitted when none is set. It is never
shown to other members or administrators.

email_verified.description: EmailVerified is true once the address was confirmed by its link.

mail_available.description:
MailAvailable is true when the server can send e-mail (SMTP is
configured): addresses can be confirmed and passwords reset by mail.

recovery_codes_remaining.description:
RecoveryCodesRemaining is how many single-use recovery codes are unused
(0 when two-factor sign-in is off).

two_factor_enabled.description: TwoFactorEnabled is true while sign-in asks for an authenticator code.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar (/api/media/{id}); omitted when none.

banned.description: Banned marks a disabled account that was banned (see GET /api/admin/bans).

banner_url.description:
BannerURL is the API URL of the profile banner (/api/media/{id}); omitted
when none and in every payload but the profile endpoints (GET
/api/users/{userID}, GET /api/auth/me and the banner routes).

locale.description: Locale is the chosen UI language ("de", "en"); empty until chosen.

login_locked.description:
LoginLocked is set while wrong passwords lock the account (or a client
address) out in memory. Only the Owner sees it set.

presence.description:
Presence is the chosen presence, only present in responses about the
caller's own account; others see the live one from the hub.

role.description:
Role is "admin" for the Owner (the one account named by ADMIN_USERNAME,
all-powerful and untouchable) and "user" for everybody else; what a user
may do beyond the defaults comes from roles (see GET /api/permissions).

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are the account's custom roles, highest first.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept) before posting, reacting, uploading or
joining a Talk. Only set in responses about the caller's own account.

status_expires_at.description:
StatusExpiresAt is when the status line clears itself; omitted when it
stays until changed.

status_text.description: StatusText is a free-text status line; empty when unset.

timeout_until.description: TimeoutUntil is set while the account is timed out.

voice_seconds.description:
Activity totals, filled where they are shown (members, profiles):
time spent in voice rooms (finished stays) and messages sent.

community_icon.description:
CommunityIcon is the version of the community icon (GET
/api/community/icon), left out while the Owner set none. Public as well.

community_name.description:
CommunityName is what the sign-in screen calls the community: the Owner's
name for it, else the host. Public, like the rest of this answer.

password_reset.description:
PasswordReset is true when members can reset a forgotten password by
e-mail (the server can send mail). It does not say who has an address.

banned_by.description: BannedBy names the moderator; empty when that account is gone.

banned_until.description: BannedUntil is null for a ban without an end.

duration_seconds.description:
DurationSeconds ends the ban by itself after that long (60 seconds to
ten years); null or missing bans for good.

reason.description:
Reason is shown to the member when they try to sign in; send an empty
string for none.

revoke_invite.description:
RevokeInvite also revokes the invite the account registered with, so
that code cannot create the account anew (default true).

only while two-factor sign-in is on.

max_uses.description: MaxUses is unlimited when null or omitted.

next_request_at.description: NextRequestAt is when a new export may be requested; omitted if now.

state.description: State is none, pending, ready, failed, downloaded or expired.

weak.description:
Weak is true for a custom code that is easy to guess (too short, a common
word). New codes like that are refused and old ones no longer work for
sign-up; regenerate them.

current.description: Current marks the session this request was made with.

device.description:
Device is a coarse label ("Firefox · Linux") parsed from the user
agent, empty when it is not recognised. No address and no raw user
agent are stored.

last_active_at.description:
LastActiveAt is when the session last made an authenticated request,
accurate to a few minutes.

push.description: Push tells whether the session's device receives Web Push notifications.

from having no open WebSocket.

computes it from the member's time zone). Omitted or null: it stays until
changed. Must lie in the future, at most a year ahead; ignored when the
status is cleared and when an admin sets another member's status.

password.description: Password is shown once; it is never stored in plain text.

duration_seconds.description: DurationSeconds is how long the member is silenced, from now.

reason.description: Reason is shown to the member. Optional.

challenge.description:
Challenge is a single-use token bound to the account and to this
sign-in; it is worth nothing without a valid code.

expires_in.description: ExpiresIn is the number of seconds the challenge stays open.

code (spaces and dashes are ignored).

security_notice.description:
SecurityNotice is set once when at least five wrong codes were entered
since the last sign-in.

otpauth_uri.description: OtpauthURI is the same secret as an otpauth:// URI, for the QR code.

secret.description: Secret is the shared secret in base32, for typing into an app by hand.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is a future time (within 8760 hours); null removes the expiry.

max_uses.description: MaxUses is at least the uses consumed so far; null (or 0) makes the invite unlimited.

display_name.description: DisplayName: empty resets it to the username.

action.description: Action is what a hit does to the message; raid protection only flags.

exempt_roles.description: ExemptRoles and ExemptChannels are skipped by the rule.

timeout_seconds.description: TimeoutSeconds, when above 0, also times the author out for that long.

domains.description: Domains (links): the domains of the lists; a domain covers its subdomains.

joins.description:
Joins and WindowSeconds (raid): more than Joins new accounts within
WindowSeconds count as a raid.

max_age_seconds.description:
MaxAgeSeconds (new_account): accounts younger than this are restricted
(60 seconds to 30 days).

max_mentions.description: MaxMentions (mentions): a message with more distinct mentions breaks the rule.

mode.description:
Mode (links): block all links, allow only the listed domains, or block
the listed domains.

restrict.description: Restrict (new_account): what a young account may not do.

restrict_seconds.description:
RestrictSeconds (raid): how long new joiners stay restricted (timed out),
60 seconds to a day.

words.description:
Words (words): blocked words and phrases, matched as whole words without
regard to case; "*" in an entry stands for any run of letters and digits.

elevated.description:
Elevated is true when the bot holds Administrator or opens any part of
the admin area: the interface warns about it.

permissions.description: Permissions are the server-wide permissions (a bit set).

allowed_intents.description: AllowedIntents are the gateway intents the bot may ask for.

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar; omitted when none.

disabled.description: Disabled bots cannot use any token or gateway connection.

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs are the bot's roles, highest first; its permissions come from
them and from channel overwrites, never from @everyone.

type.description:
Type is 4 (reply with a message) or 5 (acknowledge now, answer later
with follow-ups).

builtin.description:
Builtin marks a command the server runs itself (no bot): bot_name is
empty, and running it answers 200 with the result instead of 202.

disabled.description:
Disabled commands are hidden from members and refuse invocations; only
an admin can set it, a bot registering the command again keeps it.

Disabled commands are hidden from members and refuse invocations; only
an admin can set it, a bot registering the command again keeps it.

name.description: Name is lowercase letters, digits, '-' and '_' (1 to 32).

options.description:
Options maps option names to values: a string, a whole number, a
boolean, or the ID of a member or channel.

interaction_id.description: InteractionID identifies the run; the bot answers it.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is empty for a token that never expires.

issuer_binding.description:
IssuerBinding is only set for a token issued before 1.0, which has no
recorded issuer: "unbound" until it is first used after the upgrade,
then "inferred" (bound to the bot's creator or the Owner, whoever
qualified; regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer). Absent for a
token whose issuer was recorded when it was issued.

secret.description: Secret is the API token. It is shown only now; only its hash is kept.

choices.description:
Choices limit a string option to these values (the composer shows them
as a list). At most 25, each 1 to 100 characters.

type.description:
Type is Discord's option type: 3 string, 4 integer, 5 boolean, 6 user
(a member's ID), 7 channel (a channel ID).

flags.description:
Flags: 64 makes the response ephemeral, visible only to the member who ran
the command (never stored).

allowed_intents.description: AllowedIntents are the gateway intents the admin allowed.

id.description: ID is the bot's user ID: the author of its messages (user_id).

recorded issuer: "unbound" until it is first used after the upgrade,
then "inferred" (bound to the bot's creator or the Owner, whoever
qualified; regenerate it to bind it to its real issuer). Absent for a
token whose issuer was recorded when it was issued.

expires_at.description: ExpiresAt is optional; without it the token never expires.

days.description: Days is how long messages stay: 1, 7, 30 or 90; 0 turns auto-delete off.

parse.description:
Parse lists the kinds of mentions that notify: "users" and "everyone"
(@all and @here, which also need the Mention everyone permission).
"roles" lets @Role notify the role's members (the role must be
mentionable, or the bot must hold Mention everyone).

roles.description: Roles are role IDs (UUIDs) notified although "roles" is not in Parse.

users.description: Users are user IDs (UUIDs) notified although "users" is not in Parse.

allowed_mentions.description:
AllowedMentions limits who is notified. Default: members mentioned by
@username are, @all and @here are not.

content.description: Content is the message text (Markdown), at most 4000 characters.

message_reference.description: MessageReference quotes a message of the same channel.

parent_id.description: ParentID posts into the thread of a root message of the channel.

bot.description:
Bot is true for bot accounts, which are members too. Mention one by its
username like any member; message.mentions then lists its id.

message_id.description: MessageID is the message to quote; it must be in the same channel.

count.description: Count is how many of their latest messages (replies included), 1 to 100.

reason.description: Reason is kept in the audit log. Optional.

user_id.description: UserID is the member whose latest messages in the channel go.

auto_delete_days.description:
AutoDeleteDays removes messages older than this many days (1, 7, 30 or
90; pinned messages stay); 0 = off. Never set on direct messages.

is_lobby.description:
IsLobby marks a Talk as a "Create a Talk" lobby: joining it opens a
temporary Talk instead of taking a seat (doc/talks.md).

is_stage.description:
IsStage marks a Talk as a Stage: without talk power nobody speaks or
shares video there (doc/talks.md).

is_temp.description:
IsTemp marks a temporary Talk opened from a lobby; it is removed again
once it stays empty.

leader_id.description:
LeaderID is the leader of a temporary Talk: the member who may rename
it and set its member limit. Absent on every other channel.

number.description: Number is the channel's short, stable link number (/c/12-general).

previous_slugs.description:
PreviousSlugs are the slugs the channel had before a rename, oldest
first. Old links resolve through them; no other channel ever takes one.

slow_mode_seconds.description:
SlowModeSeconds is the least time between two messages of one member
in this channel; 0 = off. Members who may manage messages here are
exempt.

slug.description:
Slug is the channel's address in the web app (/c/general, /v/lounge):
unique server-wide, lowercase ASCII. The id stays the key everywhere.

user_limit.description:
UserLimit is the most members a voice channel admits at once; 0 = no
limit.

is_stage.description: IsStage creates the Talk as a Stage (voice channels only).

user_ids.description:
UserIDs are the other members: one for a conversation with one person,
two to nine for a group.

color.description: Color is a palette name (gray, red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple, pink); omitted means none.

moderated.description: Moderated: only members with Manage messages apply or remove the tag.

attachment_ids.description:
AttachmentIDs are files uploaded with POST /api/channels/{channelID}/attachments,
at most 10, shown in this order. Needs the Attach files permission; the
files must be the caller's, from this channel and not yet sent.

content.description: Content is required unless attachment_ids is set.

parent_id.description: ParentID must be a root message of the same channel (thread reply).

reply_to_id.description: ReplyToID must be a message of the same conversation (quoted reply).

category.description: Category is why the message is reported.

note.description: Note is an optional explanation for the moderators, up to 500 characters.

ring_seconds.description: RingSeconds is how long it keeps ringing (0 when it does not).

call.description:
Call is "invite" when the message is the card of a call and "missed"
when it records a call nobody answered; absent for any other message.

text.description: Text is the start of the message text (at most 200 characters).

list_collapsed.description: ListCollapsed is whether the member folded the sidebar section.

mute_all.description:
MuteAll silences every conversation: no push, no sound, no highlight.
Unread counts stay. A conversation's own notification setting overrides it.

reason.description:
Reason is shown to the author when a moderator deletes their message,
and kept in the audit log. Up to 200 characters.

call.description:
Call is the call going on in the conversation (absent: none). It rings
for the members who have not joined while Ringing is true. Events
dm_call_ring and dm_call_end keep it current.

can_send.description:
CanSend says whether the caller may write in it now: they hold Send
direct messages, the community has direct messages on, and no timeout
or pending rules apply. It says nothing about the other members; a
message that cannot be sent to them is refused when sent.

favourite_position.description:
FavouritePosition is the conversation's place in the caller's
favourites, 0 first (null: not a favourite).

group.description:
Group is true for a conversation that can take more members; a
conversation with one other person is not.

hidden.description:
Hidden says the caller closed the conversation in their list; the next
message written in it opens it again. It is the caller's view only.

id.description:
ID is the id messages are read and written under, in the message
routes (/api/channels/{id}/messages), which accept it for members only.

last_message.description:
LastMessage is the latest message the caller can see, for a preview
(absent: none yet). Messages of members the caller blocked are left out.

last_message_at.description: LastMessageAt is when the latest message was written (null: none yet).

members.description: Members are everybody in it, the caller included.

unread_count.description:
UnreadCount counts top-level messages of others since the caller last
read it; MentionCount those of them that mention the caller by name or
reply to them.

call.description:
Call marks the embed as the record of a call in a conversation: "missed"
is a call nobody answered (Title is the Talk's name). Only the server
sets it (dm_calls.go); webhook payloads cannot.

talk_id.description:
TalkID turns the embed into an invitation to this Talk: the client
offers a Join button. Only the server sets it (a Talk invitation,
talks_invite.go); webhook payloads cannot. Joining goes through the
ordinary permission checks, the card grants nothing.

message_id.description: MessageID is the oldest top-level message by someone else after `since`; null when there is none.

guidelines.description: Guidelines is shown above the new-post form (plain text, at most 1000 characters).

require_tag.description:
RequireTag: every post carries at least one tag (waived for a member who
may apply none, so a forum without usable tags is not closed).

color.description: Color is a name from ForumTagColors, or empty for the plain look.

moderated.description: Moderated tags are applied and removed only by members with Manage messages.

position.description: Position is the tag's place in the forum's own order (1 is first).

message_id.description: The rest is set only when Available.

channel_id.description: ChannelID is the channel or direct message conversation to forward to.

comment.description: Comment is the forwarder's own text, optional.

conversation_id.description: ConversationID is the direct message conversation to post the card into.

category_id.description: CategoryID limits the call to one category's channels; omitted or null means every channel the caller may view.

message_id.description: MessageID is the message to mark read up to; null or omitted means now.

added_by.description: AddedBy is the member who created the bot, when known.

banner_url.description:

when none and in every payload but the profile endpoints (GET
/api/users/{userID}, GET /api/auth/me and the banner routes).

built-in Bot role; webhook authors are never listed.

time spent in voice rooms (finished stays) and messages sent.

embeds.description: Embeds are the rich cards of a webhook message (Discord-style subset).

forward.description:
Forward is set when the message forwards another one. It says so and
nothing more: no id and no text of the original travels with the
message, because readers differ in what they may see. Each reader gets
the original (with its ids) from GET /api/messages/{id}/forward.

is_bot.description:
IsBot is true for messages posted by a webhook. Their author is a
hidden bot account; DisplayName is the webhook's name or the username
the sender gave for this message.

is_locked.description: IsLocked marks a forum post as locked: only moderators can post replies.

is_resolved.description: IsResolved marks a forum post as solved or answered.

is_webhook.description:
IsWebhook narrows IsBot: the author is an incoming webhook (shown with
a Webhook label), not a bot account (shown with a BOT label).

last_activity_at.description: LastActivityAt is the timestamp of the latest reply in the thread, or the post's creation time.

mention_roles.description:
MentionRoles are the roles this message mentions (@Role); the client
draws them as role pills. A role that was deleted since drops out. The
server always sends it; it is optional for clients that build messages
themselves.

mentions.description: Mentions are the users this message mentions (@username, @all, @here).

number.description: Number is the message's short, stable link number (/m/4821).

poll.description: Poll is set when the message is a poll; its content is the question.

tags.description: Tags are the forum tags attached to a forum post (up to 5 tags).

title.description: Title is the required title of a root post in a forum channel (max 100 characters).

content.description: Content is the text of this earlier version.

edited_at.description:
EditedAt is when this version was written (the message's creation time
for the original).

replaced_at.description: ReplacedAt is when an edit replaced it.

server.description: Server is the member's server-wide default (always present).

anonymous.description:
Anonymous polls never name voters: options carry counts only, and only
once the poll has ended (a running one reports 0 for every option).

closed.description: Closed is true once ClosesAt has passed, as the server saw it.

closes_at.description: ClosesAt is when voting ends; ending the poll early moves it to that moment.

multiple.description: Multiple lets a member vote for several options.

total_voters.description: TotalVoters counts members who voted for at least one option.

voters.description: Voters is only present when the poll is not anonymous.

previous_read_at.description:
PreviousReadAt is the read marker before this call (the day the caller
joined for a post never opened). Replies of others after it are unread.

dm_policy.description:
DMPolicy is everyone (the default) or nobody. It only decides who can
start a conversation with the caller or add them to a group; existing
conversations go on.

emoji.description: Emoji has no whitespace, control characters, '<' or '>'.

channel_id.description: ChannelID is the channel of the message.

tag_ids.description: TagIDs lists every tag of the forum once, in the new order.

flagged it, or raised a raid alert.

hit_count.description: HitCount counts the hits merged into an automod entry (1 for a report).

snippet.description: Snippet is the start of the root message (at most 200 characters).

ids.description:

conversation stops being one.

following.description: Following: replies of this thread notify the caller. Servers before 1.1 do not send it.
Following: replies of the thread notify the caller.

thread_id.description: ThreadID is the root message of the thread.

is_lobby.description:
IsLobby marks a voice channel as a Create-a-Talk lobby (true) or clears
the mark (false): joining a lobby opens a temporary Talk (doc/talks.md).

is_stage.description:
IsStage turns a permanent Talk into a Stage (true) or back into a normal
Talk (false); members without talk power lose their microphone, camera
and screen at once (doc/talks.md).

slow_mode_seconds.description:
SlowModeSeconds sets the least time between two messages of one member
in the channel (0 turns slow mode off). Members who may manage messages
in the channel are exempt.

user_limit.description: UserLimit caps a voice channel's members at once; 0 removes the limit.

color.description: Color is a palette name; an empty string clears it.

is_resolved.description: IsResolved marks the post as solved (author or Manage messages) or reopens it.

user_limit.description: UserLimit caps the members of the Talk at once; 0 removes the limit.

can_join.description:
CanJoin is true for a Talk the previewed member may connect to; always
false for a text channel.

permissions.description:
Permissions are the keys (GET /api/permissions) of the channel
permissions the previewed member holds here, in catalog order.

administrator.description:
Administrator is true when the role carries Administrator: such a member
sees everything the caller sees and ignores channel overwrites.

confirm_additive.description: ConfirmAdditive: the administrator confirmed what is added.

confirm_roles.description: ConfirmRoles: the administrator confirmed the role permissions.

confirm_text.description: ConfirmText is the server name or IMPORT.

role_map.description:
RoleMap maps Discord role ids onto existing role ids; those roles are
not created and keep their own permissions. It must be the map the
preview was made with.

channels_with_messages.description: ChannelsWithMessages must be confirmed separately: undoing deletes their messages.

kept_categories.description:
KeptCategories are created categories an undo leaves in place because
they now hold channels that are not part of the import.

remaining.description: Remaining are the created objects that still exist.

applied.description: Applied is reserved: @everyone is never changed, so it is always false.

dropped_bits.description: DroppedBits names every Discord permission dropped from the roles and overwrites.

hash.description: Hash identifies this exact plan; the apply request must repeat it.

mappable_roles.description:
MappableRoles are the existing roles the importer may map a Discord
role onto (highest first); the roles a role_map may name.

mapped_roles.description:
MappedRoles are the Discord roles the administrator mapped onto an
existing role: nothing is created for them.

roles.description: Roles are listed highest first; they are created below every existing role.

server_name.description: ServerName is what the third confirmation accepts besides "IMPORT".

skipped.description: Skipped lists template channels that have no counterpart (threads and the like).

category.description: Category is the name of the category it goes into ("" for none).

source_type.description: SourceType names the Discord kind it came from.

type.description: Type is the Mnema type: text, voice (a Talk), stage or forum.

mapped_role_id.description:
MappedRoleID is the existing role the overwrite is written for when the
Discord role was mapped onto one.

role_source_id.description: RoleSourceID is the template id of the role; Everyone marks @everyone.

suggested_role_id.description:
SuggestedRoleID is the existing role with the same name (ignoring case)
the administrator may map this role onto; null when there is none.

role_map.description:
RoleMap maps Discord role ids onto existing role ids: those roles are
left out of the plan and their overwrites point at the existing role.

template.description:
Template is a Discord server template link (discord.new/<code>,
discord.com/template/<code>) or the bare code.

accept_message_loss.description: AcceptMessageLoss is required when a created channel has messages now.

already_gone.description: AlreadyGone are created objects that had been deleted by hand before.

kept_categories.description: KeptCategories were left in place because they hold other channels now.

kept_roles.description:
KeptRoles counts created roles that stay because the caller can no
longer manage them (moved above their highest role since). While any
stay, the import is not marked undone and can be undone again.

animated.description: Animated emoji are GIFs and have a still frame for reduced motion.

still_url.description: StillURL is the first frame (animated emoji only).

url.description:
URL serves the image; it changes with the content (the v parameter), so
it may be cached for good.

limit.description: Limit is how many custom emoji the instance allows (EMOJI_MAX).

heartbeat_interval.description:
HeartbeatInterval is the interval the gateway will ask for, in
milliseconds (also in HELLO).

max_connections.description: MaxConnections is how many gateway connections one bot may hold.

url.description: URL is the WebSocket address of the gateway.

code.description: Code is one of the stable Code* constants; clients branch on it.

message.description: Message is a human-readable English message.

code.description:
Code is Discord's JSON error code: 0 for plain HTTP errors, 10003
unknown channel, 10008 unknown message, 50001 missing access, 50006
empty message, 50013 missing permissions, 50035 invalid form body,
40005 request entity too large.

global.description:
Global is true when the bot's overall limit was hit, false for the
limit of one route.

retry_after.description: RetryAfter is the number of seconds to wait.

remind_at.description:
RemindAt is the absolute time to remind at. The client works it out in the
member's own time zone ("tomorrow", "in 3 hours").

send_at.description:
SendAt is the absolute time to send at, worked out by the client in the
member's own time zone.

channel_name.description: ChannelName is empty for a direct message conversation.

snippet.description: Snippet is the start of the message text (up to 200 characters).

available.description:
Available is false when the caller may no longer see the message (it was
deleted, or they lost access); then Message is absent.

delivered_at.description:
DeliveredAt is set once the reminder fell due; it then waits in the list
until the caller dismisses it.

channel_name.description:
ChannelName is empty for a conversation and for a channel the caller can
no longer see.

failure_reason.description:
FailureReason is set when State is failed: slow_mode, not_allowed,
unavailable or refused.

state.description:
State is "pending" (waiting for send_at) or "failed" (the server refused
to send it; it stays as a draft the caller can edit, reschedule or delete).

send_at.description: SendAt moves the message; for a failed one it also puts it back to waiting.

author.description: Author is the channel, creator or publisher; AuthorURL links to it.

color.description: Color is the page's theme colour as #rrggbb, for a card accent.

compact.description:
Compact asks for a small thumbnail beside the text (a square avatar or
a "summary" card) instead of a wide image above it.

embed.description: Embed is set for videos the client may play inline after a click.

fields.description: Fields are short labelled facts such as a price.

image.description:
Image is the original absolute image URL; clients load it through the
image proxy because the CSP only allows same-origin images.

site_name.description: SiteName is the provider ("YouTube", "Steam", the page's og:site_name).

deleted.description: Deleted is how many were removed (cleanup only).

skipped.description: Skipped counts the old objects storage refused to delete; they stay.

raid_until.description: RaidUntil is set while raid protection is restricting newcomers.

events.description: Events is the timeline, newest first, at most the latest 200.

notes.description: Notes are the private moderator notes, newest first.

strikes.description: Strikes counts the notes marked as strikes.

actor.description: Actor is the moderator who did it; "Automod" for automod's own timeout.

added_roles.description: AddedRoles and RemovedRoles name the roles a moderator changed (roles).

duration_seconds.description: DurationSeconds is the length of a timeout or a ban with an end.

report_id.description: ReportID, Category and Status describe a report (report) or an automod hit.

rule.description:
Rule, Outcome and Hits describe an automod hit: the rule's name, what it
did and how many hits the entry counts.

can_delete.description: CanDelete: the caller wrote it, or is an Administrator.

mine.description: Mine: the caller wrote it and may edit and delete it.

strike.description: Strike counts the note in the member's strikes.

version.description: Version is the rules version the member saw (State.RulesVersion).

complete.description: Complete is true when every step that is not optional is done.

hidden.description:
Hidden is true once the Owner closed the checklist (or when the community
was already in use before the checklist existed). The server menu
reopens it.
Hidden closes (true) or reopens (false) the checklist; left out, it stays as it is.

visited.description: Visited are steps the Owner has now opened: channels, status. They are added, never removed.

id.description: ID names the step (name, invite, channels, voice, status, roles_rules).

optional.description: Optional steps do not count towards Complete.

community_icon.description:
CommunityIcon is the version of the community icon (GET
/api/community/icon), empty while none is set. It changes with every
upload. Set with PUT /api/admin/community/icon, not with the settings.

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled is the community's switch for direct messages
(default on). Off: existing conversations stay readable and members
can neither start new ones nor write in them.

rules_text.description: RulesText is Markdown. Empty means no rules: nothing is enforced.

rules_version.description:
RulesVersion counts the published versions of the rules (0: never set).
Members must have accepted it before they may post, react, upload or
join a Talk (only while RulesText is not empty).

session_inactivity_days.description:
SessionInactivityDays is how many days without an authenticated request
sign a session out (1 to 365, default 7). Inactivity, not age.

start_channel_id.description:
StartChannelID is the text channel new members land in; null for the
first channel they can see.

welcome_text.description: WelcomeText is Markdown, shown to new members first.

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled switches direct messages on or off for the
community; left out, it stays as it is.

require_reacceptance.description:
RequireReacceptance raises the rules version, so every member (the Owner
excepted) has to accept the rules again. The first time rules are
written the version is raised on its own. Ignored while the rules are
empty.

session_inactivity_days.description:
SessionInactivityDays sets the inactivity sign-out (1 to 365 days); left
out, it stays as it is. It applies to running sessions at once.

dismissed_tips.description: DismissedTips are the tips the member closed.

rules_accepted_version.description: RulesAcceptedVersion is the version the member accepted last.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is true while the member has to accept the rules; until
then posting, reacting, uploading and joining a Talk answer
RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED. Never true for the Owner.

rules_version.description: RulesVersion is the version in force; 0 while there are no rules.

start_channel_id.description:
StartChannelID is the channel to open after the welcome flow; null when
none is set or the member cannot view it.

welcome_done.description: WelcomeDone is true once the member finished the welcome flow.

dismissed_tips.description: DismissedTips are tip ids to add (at most 32 per call, 64 stored).

welcome_done.description: WelcomeDone marks the welcome flow finished.

count.description: Count is how often it was raised since then (for runtime warnings).

since.description: Since is when the warning was first raised in this process.

value.description: Value is an optional non-sensitive number (e.g. the UDP port count).

channel.description:
Channel permissions can be overwritten per category and channel; the
rest only apply server-wide.

id.description: ID is the role's or the member's ID; the @everyone role is a role.

type.description: Type is what ID refers to.

bot_user_id.description:
BotUserID is set on a bot's own managed role: the account of the one bot
that holds it. The role is named after the bot and goes with it.

description.description: Description says in a line what the role is for; the member picker shows it.

max_upload_mb.description:
MaxUploadMB overrides the upload limit of this role's members; null
inherits the global limit. A member gets the highest override of their
roles (@everyone included), never above the server's ceiling.

self_assignable.description:
SelfAssignable lets every member add or remove this role on their own
account. Only roles without Administrator or admin-area permissions can be
flagged, never @everyone or a managed role. Omitted when false.

description.description: Description is one line shown to members choosing roles.

max_upload_mb.description:
MaxUploadMB: absent leaves it alone, null inherits the global limit, a
number sets the role's limit. Only the Owner may send it.

self_assignable.description:
SelfAssignable lets members add and remove the role themselves; refused
for @everyone, managed roles and roles with Administrator or admin-area permissions.

ceiling_mb.description: CeilingMB is the operator's hard ceiling (MAX_UPLOAD_SIZE_MB).

max_upload_mb.description: MaxUploadMB is the effective global limit.

anonymous.description:
Anonymous stores only that a member voted and the count per option, never
the choice; a vote in it cannot be changed. Offered with the polls.anonymous feature.

duration.description: Duration is how long voting stays open; 24h when omitted.

multiple.description: Multiple lets members vote for several options.

anonymous.description:
Anonymous polls never name voters: options carry counts only, and only
once the poll has ended (a running one reports 0 for every option).

closed.description: Closed is true once ClosesAt has passed, as the server saw it.

closes_at.description: ClosesAt is when voting ends; ending the poll early moves it to that moment.

has_voted.description: HasVoted says that the caller voted, also in an anonymous poll.

multiple.description: Multiple lets a member vote for several options.

my_votes.description:
MyVotes are the options the caller voted for. It is always empty in an
anonymous poll, which does not know the choice.

total_voters.description: TotalVoters counts members who voted for at least one option.

option_ids.description: OptionIDs replace the caller's votes; an empty list withdraws them.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when the operator turned push off (PUSH_ENABLED=false).

max_devices.description: MaxDevices is how many devices one account may enable push on.

preview.description: Preview is the member's choice: include the message text in pushes. Only takes effect while PreviewAllowed.

preview_allowed.description: PreviewAllowed is false when the operator forces pushes without message text.

public_key.description: PublicKey is the VAPID public key (base64url) to subscribe with; empty while push is off.

preview.description: Preview includes the message text in pushes (default true).

auth.description: Auth is the browser's 16 byte authentication secret, base64url.

endpoint.description: Endpoint is the push service address the browser got. https only, a public host, port 443.

label.description: Label names the device in the list ("Firefox on Windows"); at most 64 characters.

p256dh.description: P256dh is the browser's P-256 public key, base64url.

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are all custom roles the member should have.

channels.description:
Channels lists every channel the caller may view with what they may do
there (bits).

direct_messages_enabled.description:
DirectMessagesEnabled is the community's switch for direct messages;
CanStartDirectMessages says whether the caller may start them and write
in them now (the switch is on, they hold Send direct messages, and no
timeout or pending rules apply).

max_upload_mb.description:
MaxUploadMB is the largest file the caller may upload, in MB: their
roles' override or the global limit, never above the server's ceiling.
It changes with permissions_changed.

owner.description:
Owner is true for the Owner, who may do everything and cannot be
restricted.

permissions.description: Permissions are the server-wide permissions (bits, see catalog).

role_ids.description: RoleIDs are the caller's custom roles, highest first.

rules_pending.description:
RulesPending is set while the caller has to accept the community rules
(POST /api/onboarding/accept); posting, reacting, uploading and joining
a Talk answer RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED until then.

timeout_until.description:
TimeoutUntil and TimeoutReason are set while the caller is timed out:
they can read but not post, react, speak or join Talks. The reason is
the moderator's, and the caller's own to see.

top_position.description:
TopPosition is the position of the caller's highest role (0 without
one); the Owner is above every position. A member can only manage roles
and members below it.

role_ids.description:
RoleIDs lists every custom role (not @everyone) exactly once, highest
first.

max_upload_mb.description: MaxUploadMB is the new global limit; null returns to the server's ceiling.

allocations.description: Allocations are the relayed sessions open now.

enabled.description:
Enabled is whether the setting asks for the relay now; Active whether it
is running and offered to members.

host.description:
Host is the name members are told to reach the relay at (from
PUBLIC_URL); empty when none is known.

mode.description:
Mode is the setting: auto (on while no external TURN is configured),
on or off.

port.description: Port is the UDP and TCP port it is configured to listen on.

reachability.description:
Reachability is a best-effort self-test from this machine to Host:Port:
reachable, unreachable (also what a router without NAT loopback shows
for a forwarded port) or unknown (not run, or nothing to test).

udp.description:
UDP and TCP say which transports are listening; one can fail to bind
while the other works.

basis.description:
Basis is "observed" when this host's own cost per packet was used,
"table" when the benchmark values were (too little traffic).

more_members.description:
MoreMembers: each one watching a 1.5 Mbit/s screen share, planning at
half of the CPU. 0 with Status memory or busy.

per_member_millicores.description: PerMemberMillicores is the CPU one more member costs.

plan_cores.description: PlanCores is the CPU the estimate allows itself to use.

scale.description: Scale is this host's observed CPU cost divided by the model's.

status.description: Status is ok, busy (past the plan already) or memory (RSS near the limit).

collecting.description:
Collecting is true in the first seconds after the start, before the
sampler has taken a measurement: the figures are not real yet.

cpu_cores.description:
CPUCores is the CPU the server may use; CPUUsedCores what it used over
the last minute.

egress_mbps.description: EgressMbps is the media the server sends, averaged over the last minute.

estimate.description: Estimate is the planning estimate (see doc/benchmark.md).

memory_limit_bytes.description: MemoryLimitBytes is the container limit (APP_MEM_LIMIT); 0 when unknown.

peers.description: Peers are media connections now; ScreenShares live screen shares.

sdp.description: SDP is the server's answer with all of its candidates.

SDP is the browser's offer: one data channel and no audio or video,
with all of its candidates gathered.

latest_migration.description: LatestMigration is the newest applied migration file, e.g. "0012_message_count.sql".

pending_migrations.description:
PendingMigrations counts embedded migrations not applied yet (0 when
the server started normally: it migrates before serving).

community_icon.description:
CommunityIcon is the version of the community icon the Owner set, left
out while there is none. GET /api/community/icon serves it (public); the
version changes with every upload, so a client refetches when it differs
from the one it has.

community_name.description:
CommunityName is what this server calls itself: the name the Owner set
in the welcome settings, else the host it is served from. It is public
on purpose, so a client can label a server before anyone signs in.

features.description:
Features lists the optional features this server has, so a web app of a
newer release can hide what an older server lacks (for example "blocks").
A server of 1.0.x sends no list. See doc/api-stability.md.

web_client_api.description: WebClientAPI identifies the HTTPS web-client desktop integration contract.

credential.description: Credential is set for TURN only and valid for 12 hours.

username.description: Username is set for TURN only.

address_detection.description:
AddressDetection is true when the server may ask public STUN servers
for its own address at startup (WEBRTC_AUTO_ANNOUNCE); ClockCheck is
true when it compares its clock with NTP servers (CLOCK_CHECK_ENABLED).
Both reveal only the server's IP address.

builtin_turn.description:
BuiltinTURN is true when the TURN relay inside the server process is
offered to members (WEBRTC_BUILTIN_TURN); the policy then describes it
as part of this server. TURNServers lists the external ones.

media_retention_days.description: MediaRetentionDays is 0 when media is kept until deleted manually.

update_check.description:
UpdateCheck is true when the server asks GitHub for new releases
(UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED); the privacy policy then names the connection.

configured.description: Configured is true when SMTP_HOST is set.

from.description: From is the sender address of outgoing mail; empty when not configured.

tls.description: TLS is the transport security in use (starttls, tls or none); empty when not configured.

setup.description:
Setup is the setup checklist: green, amber and red items, each red or
amber one naming the variable to set.

waited.description: Waited counts acquisitions that had to wait for a free connection.

cpu_millicores.description: CPUMillicores is process CPU use over the interval, 1000 = one core.

egress_pps.description: EgressPPS and IngressPPS are RTP packets per second over the interval.

t.description: T is the unix time in seconds.

history.description: History holds up to the last hour of samples, oldest first.

interval_seconds.description: IntervalSeconds is the spacing of History.

mem_alloc_bytes.description:
MemAllocBytes is live heap memory; MemSysBytes what the Go runtime
obtained from the OS.

password.description: Password is the admin's current password (re-authentication).

target_version.description:
TargetVersion must equal the latest release the server knows, so a
dialog opened before a newer release can't start the wrong update.

available.description:
Available: configured, an update exists, the image can reach it and no
update ran in the last five minutes.

configured.description: Configured is true when UPDATER_TOKEN is set (sidecar opted in).

image.description: Image is MNEMA_IMAGE, the image reference the app container runs.

next_allowed_at.description: NextAllowedAt is set during the cooldown after an update request.

reach.description: Reach says whether re-pulling Image can reach the latest release.

usage_unavailable.description:
UsageUnavailable is true when the usage could not be read in time; the
counts above are then zero because they are unknown.

mail.description: Mail is the outgoing mail setup (account e-mails need it).

warnings.description:
Warnings are configuration or deployment problems the server noticed
(stable codes; the web app explains each). Empty when all is well.

current.description: Current is the release version ("dev" for a build without one).

revision.description: Revision is the short git commit of the build; empty when unknown.

to.description: To is the recipient; it defaults to the Owner's own e-mail address.

check_enabled.description: CheckEnabled is false with UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED=false (no requests to GitHub).

check_error.description: CheckError says why the last check failed (empty when it worked).

latest_version.description: LatestVersion is empty until a check succeeded.

release_notes.description: ReleaseNotes is Markdown; clients render it as untrusted text.

release_url.description: ReleaseURL is the release page on github.com.

retry_at.description: RetryAt is set while GitHub's rate limit pauses the checks.

builtin_turn.description: BuiltinTURN reports the TURN relay built into the server.

enabled.description: Enabled is false when the SFU could not start (voice disabled).

media_connections.description: MediaConnections are the SFU's peer connections.

rooms.description: Rooms and Participants are the calls as members see them.

turn_configured.description:
TURNConfigured is true when members are offered any TURN relay: the
external one (WEBRTC_TURN_URLS) or the one built into the server.

websocket_connections.description:
WebSocketConnections are open realtime connections; OnlineUsers the
distinct users behind them.

connected.description:
Connected is whether the admin's own /api/ws connection is open and
upgraded.

code.description:
Code names the outcome ("public_url.local"): clients translate by it and
fill in Params. Absent when the server has no code for the outcome.

detail.description:
Detail says what was found, in one sentence, in English; the fallback
for clients that do not know the Code.

fix.description: Fix names the variable to set and the value to use, in English; empty when ok.

id.description: ID is the stable identifier of the check.

level.description:
Level is ok (green), info (neutral: not verifiable from here), warn
(amber) or fail (red).

params.description: Params are the values the message names (ports, variable values), by name.

parse.description:
Parse lists the kinds of mentions that notify: "users" and "everyone"
(@all and @here) and "roles" (@Role).

roles.description:
Roles are role IDs (UUIDs) that are notified although "roles" is not
in Parse.

users.description:
Users are user IDs (UUIDs) that are notified although "users" is not in
Parse.

url.description:
URL receives the events: http or https, public addresses only unless
the operator allowed more (WEBHOOK_ALLOW_PRIVATE_TARGETS).

channel_id.description:
ChannelID is the channel the webhook belongs to; it receives that
channel's events only.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy is the member who created it, kept for the record (null once
that account is gone). It grants nothing.

events.description: Events are the subscribed event types (see doc/webhooks.md).

last_error.description:
LastError is a short code for the latest failure ("timeout",
"blocked_address", "http_500", ...); null after a success.

last_status.description:
LastStatus is the HTTP status of the latest attempt (null: none yet, or
no response).

secret.description: Secret signs every delivery (see X-Mnema-Signature in doc/webhooks.md).

status.description:
Status is "active", "disabled" (switched off by a member) or
"auto_disabled" (switched off after repeated failures).

url_set_by.description:
URLSetBy and URLSetAt record who last set the URL and when, so stale
webhooks are easy to spot. The URL receives the channel's events until an
administrator changes or deletes the webhook.

allow_attachments.description: AllowAttachments lets a post carry files (default on).

allow_embeds.description: AllowEmbeds lets a post carry embeds (default on).

allow_everyone.description:
AllowEveryone lets @all and @here notify people (default off). It also
takes "everyone" in the sender's allowed_mentions.

allow_identity_override.description:
AllowIdentityOverride lets a post set its own username (default on).
Avatars from other hosts are never used.

allow_user_mentions.description:
AllowUserMentions lets @username notify members (default on, as Discord
does with allowed_mentions.parse = users).

avatar_url.description: AvatarURL is the API URL of the avatar; omitted when none is set.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy is the administrator who created it, kept for the record (null
once that account is gone). It grants nothing.

token.description:
Token is the secret part of the URL. It is stored hashed and cannot be
shown again; regenerate the token to get a new URL.

url.description: URL is the full execute URL, token included.

error.description: Error is a short code, never the response or the raw network error.

code.description:
Code is Discord's JSON error code (10015 unknown webhook, 50027 invalid
token, 50006 empty message, 50035 invalid form body, ...).

global.description: Global is always false: limits are per webhook and per channel.

retry_after.description: RetryAfter is the number of seconds to wait.

allowed_mentions.description:
AllowedMentions limits who is notified. Default: members mentioned by
@username are, @all and @here are not.

avatar_url.description:
AvatarURL is accepted and ignored: Mnema Talk never loads pictures from
other hosts. Set the avatar on the webhook instead.

content.description: Content is the message text (Markdown), at most 4000 characters.

username.description: Username overrides the webhook's name for this message.

channel_id.description:
ChannelID is the channel the webhook belongs to; it receives that
channel's events only.

created_by.description:
CreatedBy is the member who created it, kept for the record (null once
that account is gone). It grants nothing.

events.description: Events are the subscribed event types (see doc/webhooks.md).

last_error.description:
LastError is a short code for the latest failure ("timeout",
"blocked_address", "http_500", ...); null after a success.

last_status.description:
LastStatus is the HTTP status of the latest attempt (null: none yet, or
no response).

status.description:
Status is "active", "disabled" (switched off by a member) or
"auto_disabled" (switched off after repeated failures).

url_set_by.description:

info.description:
REST API of Mnema Talk, a self-hosted, invite-only chat and voice app for a single community.
Authentication is an HttpOnly session cookie set by login/register. State-changing requests (anything but GET/HEAD/OPTIONS) must carry a same-origin Origin header, otherwise 403.
JSON bodies are decoded strictly: unknown fields are rejected with 400 and bodies are limited to 1 MiB. Errors share the ErrorResponse shape.
Everything except the SPA assets lives under /api.
Conventions. Creating returns 201 with the new object; a delete or a change without a result returns 204 with no body, while a few operations return 200 with the changed object (for example timing out a member or unpinning a message), as their descriptions say.
Every 429 carries a Retry-After header (seconds). Lists that page do so with `limit` and, depending on the list, `before` / `after` (an id) or a cursor; each operation names its parameters and maximum.
Uploads are the one exception to the 1 MiB body limit; their size limits are on the operations.
A 403 names its cause in the message: a missing permission (named on the operation), a role that is not below yours, or a cross-origin request refused by the Origin / Sec-Fetch-Site check.
A 403 with the code RULES_NOT_ACCEPTED means the member has not accepted the community rules yet. It is returned by every operation that posts, reacts, uploads or joins a Talk (sending messages and polls, voting, reactions, uploads, slash commands); accept the rules with POST /api/onboarding/accept first.

get.description:
Upgrades to a WebSocket (requires a same-origin Origin header; a foreign origin is refused with 403 by the upgrade handler). OpenAPI cannot model WebSocket frames, so the protocol is described here.

Every frame in both directions is a JSON text message `{"type": string, "payload": any}`. At most a few events per second per connection (and per account across its connections) are processed; excess client events, and events whose payload is over the cap for their type (1 KiB, more only for an SDP answer, ICE candidate, diagnostic and media handshake), are dropped.

Server to client, on connect (to this connection only):
- `presence_snapshot`: map of user id to live status for every online user.
- `voice_snapshot`: map of voice channel id to a map of user id to User plus `joined_at`.
- `voice_rooms`: `{started: {channelId: time}, now}`; the server clock lets clients count up.

Server to client, broadcast to all connections:
Channel events (`message_*`, `typing`, `voice_state_update`, `webrtc_media_state`) only reach connections whose user may view that channel; the connect snapshots list only the Talks the user may view.
- `message_create`, `message_update`: Message.
- `message_delete`: `{id, channel_id, parent_id}`.
- `message_reaction`: `{message_id, channel_id, reactions}`.
- `channels_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/channels (sent after any category/channel/layout admin change).
- `permissions_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/permissions and GET /api/channels. Sent to the users whose roles or permissions may have changed (everybody after a channel, category, overwrite or @everyone change).
- `roles_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/roles and GET /api/members (a role was created, edited, deleted, reordered or assigned).
- `emoji_changed`: no payload; refetch GET /api/emoji (a custom emoji was added, renamed or deleted).
- `member_joined`: public User of a newly registered member.
- `user_update`: public User after a profile, status or avatar change, or `{id, disabled}` when an admin disables or enables an account.
- `user_stats`: `{user_id, voice_seconds}` after a voice stay ends.
- `presence_update`: `{user_id, status}` where status is online, away, dnd, focus or offline; for a bot that set an activity also `activity: {type, name}` (Discord activity type).
- `voice_state_update`: `{action: "join", channel_id, user, started_at}` or `{action: "leave", channel_id, user_id}`.
- `typing`: `{channel_id, user_id}` (to everyone except the typist).

Server to client, targeted:
- `block_updated`: to the user's own sessions only; `{user_id, blocked}` after they blocked or unblocked a member (refetch GET /api/me/blocks). The blocked member is never told.
- `dm_created`: to every member's sessions; the direct message (`DirectMessage`) a conversation was started with, or the one the receiver was just added to.
- `dm_member_added`: to the other members of a group conversation; `{dm_id, member}`.
- `dm_member_removed`: to the remaining members and the leaver's sessions; `{dm_id, member}`.
- `dm_prefs_updated`: to the user's own sessions only; `{dm_id}` after they closed, reopened or (un)favourited a conversation (refetch GET /api/dms/{id}), or `{dm_id: null}` after their direct message settings changed (refetch GET /api/dms).
- `dm_call_ring`: to the members' sessions that asked for conversations (`?dm=1`), the caller's own included; `{conversation_id, talk_id, message_id, caller_id, talk_name, ring_seconds}` after a Talk was started from, or shared into, a conversation. Everyone but the caller has an incoming call for `ring_seconds` (counted from receipt), unless a `dm_call_end` comes first. Additive: a client that ignores it still gets the invitation card as `message_create`.
- `dm_call_end`: to the same sessions; `{conversation_id, talk_id, reason, active, user_id?, message_id?}` when the call stopped ringing. `reason` is `answered` (a member other than the caller entered the Talk; `user_id` says who, so their other devices and the other members drop the incoming call), `cancelled` (the caller left before anybody joined, or started another Talk in the conversation), `timeout` (nobody joined in time) or `ended` (the last member left). `active` is true while somebody is still in the Talk. After `cancelled` and `timeout` the server has posted a "missed call" message (an embed with `call: "missed"`, written by the caller; `message_id`), announced by `message_create` just before.
- `talk_leader`: `{channel_id, leader_id}` to everyone who may view a temporary Talk (opened from a Create-a-Talk lobby) when its leader changes; `leader_id` is null when nobody leads it.
- `talk_moved`: `{from_channel_id, channel_id}` to the connection whose `voice_join` of a Create-a-Talk lobby opened the temporary Talk `channel_id`; the client then sends its ordinary `voice_join` for that Talk. The connection is never seated in the lobby itself.
- `read_state`: to the user's own sessions only; `{channel_id, last_read_at, unread_count, mention_count}`, `{channel_id, last_read_at, refresh: true}`, or `{refresh: true}` alone after a notification setting changed or everything was marked read (reload read states and notification settings).
- `webrtc_media_state`: `{channel_id, user_id, screen, camera}` to voice-room members.
- `voice_speaking`: `{channel_id, user_id, active}` to voice-room members, only when the state changes.
- `screen_viewers`: `{channel_id, user_id, viewers}` to voice-room members: `viewers` are the distinct users in the room watching `user_id`'s screen share (sorted ids, never the sharer). Sent whenever that set changes (`viewers: []` once when a watched share ends or loses its last viewer), and on `voice_join` one per live share to the joining connection only.
- `webrtc_offer` (SDP offer), `webrtc_candidate` (ICE candidate): SFU signalling.
- `screen_layers`: `{channel_id, user_id, layers}` to voice-room members: the layers of `user_id`'s live screen share, best first, each `{width, height, fps}` as the sharer declared them. Sent when they change, as an empty list once the share ends, and on `voice_join` one per live share to the joining connection only. A share of a client without layers has none.
- `screen_quality`: `{channel_id, user_id, layer, auto}` to the watching connection only: the layer of `user_id`'s screen share it receives now (`-1` before the first picture) and whether the server chooses it (`auto`).
- `cameras_capped`: `{channel_id, user_ids}` to the viewing connection only: whose cameras the server does not forward because the viewer asked for more than 24 at once (the lowest user ids are forwarded). Sent when that set changes, as an empty list once nothing is capped; the client shows those tiles without a picture.
- `screen_layers_wanted`: `{channel_id, layers, source?}` to the sharing connection only: the indexes of its layers some viewer receives or is about to (`source: "camera"` for the layers of its camera, absent for its screen share). A sender may stop encoding the others; layer 0 is always listed while nobody watches.
- `media_handshake`: `{channel_id, user_id, wire}` to the other connections in that voice room. `wire` is opaque: the server checks only its framing (an MLS key package, welcome or public message, or a heartbeat or capability message) and never reads or logs the content.
- `voice_kicked`: `{channel_id, reason?}` when a moderator removes the user from voice, `reason: "room_full"` when a voice join is refused because the room is full (the channel's `user_limit`; members with Disconnect members in that Talk, Administrators and the Owner may exceed it), `reason: "rules_not_accepted"` when the community's rules have not been accepted yet (POST /api/onboarding/accept), `reason: "talk_rate_limited"` or `"talk_unavailable"` when joining a Create-a-Talk lobby opened no Talk (5 new Talks per 10 minutes and member, 50 open Talks per lobby), or `reason: "connection_lost"` when the media connection of the call failed and the server dropped it (join again), `reason: "media_unavailable"` when the media connection of a join could not be set up (the seat is given up; join again), `reason: "joined_elsewhere"` to a connection whose Talk the same account joined on another connection (one connection per account and Talk holds the media), `reason: "voice_taken_over"` to a connection whose voice (in any Talk) the same account moved to another connection with `voice_join` and `takeover: true`; only its voice ends, the WebSocket stays open, or `reason: "missing_permission"` when the user may not (or no longer may) view and connect to that Talk.
- `pong`: `{t}` echoing a `ping`.

Client to server:
- `ping` `{t}`; `presence_idle` `{idle: bool}`.
- `typing` `{channel_id}` (text and voice channels, rate-limited; ignored without View channels and Send messages).
- `voice_join` `{channel_id, takeover?, resume?, tab?}` (needs View channels and Connect, otherwise `voice_kicked` with `reason: "missing_permission"`). Without `takeover`, the account's other connection in the same Talk is told `joined_elsewhere` and a connection in another Talk keeps its seat. With `takeover: true` (the client sends it after the user confirmed "take over here") the join is completed first and only then does every other connection of the account leave voice, each told `voice_taken_over`; of two takeovers at once the later seat wins. A client that reconnected sends `resume: true` to continue its call, and `tab`, an id its page keeps across reconnects (up to 64 characters): if a takeover ended that page's call and another connection of the account is in voice, it is answered with `voice_kicked` `voice_taken_over` instead of taking the voice back; `voice_leave`; `voice_speaking` `{active}`. The SFU drops audio without Speak and camera/screen without Video.
- `webrtc_answer` (SDP answer), `webrtc_candidate` (ICE candidate), `webrtc_request_keyframe` (optionally `{source: "screen"|"camera"}`: a keyframe of the sender's own video of that source, e.g. after a camera change, so its viewers get a fresh picture; without it, of the videos the sender watches).
- `media_handshake` `{channel_id, wire}`: opaque handshake bytes for the current voice room.
- `webrtc_subscribe` `{kind: "screen"|"camera", user_id, on}`, `{kind: "camera", all: true, on}` or `{kind: "camera", user_ids: [up to 16 ids], on}` (several cameras with one renegotiation; a client that shows only some cameras asks for just those). A screen subscription may carry `quality`: `"auto"` or the index of a layer (0 is the best); it is applied before the first picture and again whenever sent. Without one, or with `"auto"`, the server chooses: it starts on the best layer, moves down one layer at a time when the viewer's receiver reports show lasting loss, a rising round trip time or repeated keyframe requests, and tries one layer up again after a long stretch without trouble (a failed attempt makes the next one wait twice as long). A camera subscription may carry `fit_px` (0 to 16384): how tall in device pixels the viewer's picture of that camera is; the server then gives it the smallest layer of a camera sent as layers that still has the pixels, and the message changes nothing else (it is sent only to a server whose `server_info` has `camera_layers`).
- `webrtc_layers` `{layers: [{width, height, fps}, ...]}` (1 to 3, best first, strictly shrinking): the layers of the sender's own screen share, or of its camera with `source: "camera"` (declared before its first video; a camera without layers is one plain track). They are sent on the SFU's lower video lines.
- `webrtc_screenshare_stop`, `webrtc_camera_stop`.

Unknown event types are ignored. The server closes the connection when the session is revoked (sign-out of that session, sign-out everywhere, password change) or expires, or the account is disabled. A user keeps at most 8 browser connections: a newer one closes the oldest with close code 4001 ("too many connections"), after which that client should not reconnect by itself. Upgrades are rate-limited per address and per user (429), and `voice_join` beyond about one per second (burst 3) is answered with `voice_kicked`.
